The best performance by a Club man was that of Sid Warboys, who finished second to Harry Payne, the Marathon champion, in a scratch 13½ miles road race.
Warboys, who some had fancied to win the title, did not start as he was away on holiday. This was Allum's first Club Championship, although he had been very close on the country in the past.

Then came Warboys, Nuti, of the "Valley," Robertshaw, Dewberry, Carter, with a sprained ankle, Fletcher, who passed six in the last mile, Browning (Ashcombe), Smith, at last finding a bit of form, and Joe Flower.
In the breakaway two things were very noticeable, the lead gained by Joe Flower over the rest of the field, and the waiting tactics adopted by Sid Warboys.
Warboys led the field for a short time, as he did in last year's National, but he soon relinquished it to Harman, the former International. About the same time Allum and Ferris moved up to second.

At the start, Dewberry, Warboys and Allum sprang into the lead and were joined by Jack Flower before reaching the "village"; Allum, however, soon moved into first position and maintained it the whole way, gradually but steadily increasing the lead.
Our next men home were Warboys (16th), Penny (18th), Footer (33rd) (a really wonderful effort this, after a very short preparation), Jack Flower (38th), and Duffett (52nd).
